# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 39 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 39 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_039_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 6, Part 1 — On the Two Ways and the Two Angels

**39:1** "I commanded you," he said, "in the first commandment to keep faith and fear and self-control." "Yes, lord," I said. "But now," he said, "I wish to show you the powers of these commandments, that you may know what power each one has and what it works."

**39:2** "There are two angels with man," he said, "one of righteousness and one of wickedness." "How then, lord," I said, "shall I know their workings, since both dwell with me?"

**39:3** "Listen," he said, "and understand them. The angel of righteousness is delicate and modest and gentle and calm. When therefore he ascends into your heart, immediately he speaks with you concerning righteousness, purity, holiness, self-control, and every righteous deed and every glorious virtue. When all these things ascend into your heart, know that the angel of righteousness is with you. These are the works of the angel of righteousness. Trust him therefore and his works."

**39:4** "Now look at the works of the angel of wickedness also. First of all, he is wrathful and bitter and foolish, and his works are evil and overthrow the servants of God. When therefore he ascends into your heart, know him by his works."

**39:5** "How I shall discern him, lord," I said, "I do not know." "Listen," he said. "When a fit of anger or bitterness comes upon you, know that he is in you. Then also the desire for many deeds and the extravagance of many foods and drunken bouts and various and unnecessary pleasures, and the desire for women, and avarice and excessive pride and boastfulness, and whatever things are like these and similar to these — when therefore these things ascend into your heart, know that the angel of wickedness is in you."

**39:6** "Since then you know his works, keep away from him and trust him not at all, because his works are evil and unprofitable for the servants of God. Here then you have the works of both angels. Understand them and trust the angel of righteousness."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the paratactic style and word order of Hermas wherever possible.*
